subject: Pilot evaluation — implementation agreements & timeline
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@brightline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot evaluation — implementation agreements & timeline

Anna — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list to share with your team.

High-level outcome we discussed:
- Brightline wants a 4-week pilot to validate retrieval-augmented generation for product search (goal: +15% conversion on query completions) with production-like traffic replay.

Proposed success criteria (for agreement):
- Functional: API integration with our query enrichment + tool-calls working end-to-end (search -> LLM -> rerank)
- Performance: average token-generation latency <= 220ms; 99th percentile < 450ms under replayed load of 50 qps
- Quality: top-3 result relevance lift >= 12% on your internal eval set
- Cost: token unit cost target within your committed cap (we’ll surface per-route costing)

Immediate asks for kickoff:
1) Provide a small sample of production queries + gold labels (attachment ok).
2) Confirm sandbox credentials (we can create a temporary sandbox key and scoped project).
3) Pick an internal tech owner to work with Karthik (we’ll cc them on the integration checklist).

Proposed timeline (flexible):
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on success criteria, share sample data and access
- Week 1: SDK integration + basic generate/embeddings routes wired; smoke tests
- Week 2: streaming/tool-calling flows and retriever integration; replay testing begins
- Week 3: metric collection, tuning (batching, cache), QA
- Week 4: acceptance run and handoff (decision on next steps)

I’ve attached a short POC checklist that we typically use to make sure nothing is missed. Karthik will be our engineering lead on the Redwood side; Marissa will handle coordination and product-level acceptance.

Attachments: redwood_poc-checklist.pdf

Next step: if that looks good, can you confirm your preferred kickoff date and who on your engineering team will be the day-to-day contact?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

We can do kickoff on May 22 or May 24 — prefer May 22 if Redwood can provide a short 30m technical alignment session beforehand with Karthik.

On the API contract: please include an example for streaming token outputs and an example for function/tool calls (we plan to call your reranker as a tool). A simple SDK snippet would help our engineers start.

Thanks,
Anna Lopez

Anna — thanks for the speed. Quick answers and a technical sketch to unblock Marcus and your engineers.

Data retention / security:
- During the pilot we retain logs for 30 days by default; we can extend or set automatic purges per your requirements. We’ll provide a SOC2 summary and the minimum set of logs we collect (request/response hashes, timing) to your security team.

API / SDK outline (we’ll share full docs and sample repo):
- Core routes you’ll use: POST /v1/generate (sync), POST /v1/generate?stream=true (server-sent events or websocket), POST /v1/embeddings, POST /v1/rerank (tool-call endpoint)
- Tool calling: we support structured tool-calls where the model returns a JSON action; Redwood runtime will invoke your retriever/reranker endpoint via a short-lived signed callback if you choose managed tool-call mode.
- Auth: standard bearer token; we can provision a scoped sandbox key limited to the pilot project.

Minimal streaming example (Python SDK style):

from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY")
for chunk in client.generate_stream(project_id="brightline-poc", prompt=prompt):
    print(chunk.text, end='')

(we'll include fuller snippets in the repo)

Operational knobs we recommend for the pilot:
- Start with batch_size=8 and adjust after initial replay runs
- Enable prefix/KV caching on stable sessions (significant cost win for product search workloads)
- If you have long contexts, we’ll test 8-bit quantized variants to see latency/cost trade-offs

I’ve attached our short POC checklist; Karthik will own the technical delivery and will schedule a 30-minute alignment session ahead of kickoff.

Attachments: redwood_poc-checklist.pdf

- Aditya

Date: 2028-05-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot evaluation — implementation agreements & timeline

Marcus / Anna — Karthik here (Redwood engineering). Short implementation plan and dev estimates so you can slot this into your sprint.

High-level integration tasks (priority order):
1) Sandbox provisioning & auth (1 day) — Redwood creates project + sandbox key, you verify access.
2) Wire basic generate + embeddings (2-3 days) — validate shapes and auth.
3) Retriever/reranker tool-call integration (2-4 days) — we’ll show an example signed callback; your reranker should accept a JSON payload and return a ranked list.
4) Streaming & long-context tuning (2 days) — test SSE/websocket path and KV cache behavior.
5) Replay and load verification (2-3 days) — run your 50 qps replay and observe latencies.

Estimated engineering effort: ~8–12 engineer-days from Brightline (depends on how much of the retriever you already have) + Redwood support during replay windows.

Implementation checklist (excerpt):
- [ ] Sandbox key provisioned
- [ ] /v1/generate wired with sample prompt and basic validation
- [ ] /v1/rerank tool-call endpoint reachable from Redwood (IP allowlist or signed callback)
- [ ] Streaming path validated (client receives SSE events in order)
- [ ] Replay script and load harness scheduled
- [ ] Metric dashboards configured (latency, tokens, cost per route)

Python SDK quick-start (example):

from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
# sync generate
resp = client.generate(project_id="brightline-poc", prompt="Search: wireless headphones")
print(resp.choices[0].text)

# streaming (pseudo)
for event in client.generate_stream(project_id="brightline-poc", prompt=prompt):
    if event.type == 'token':
        print(event.token, end='')
    elif event.type == 'tool_call':
        # tool call flow: call your reranker, return JSON
        pass

Notes / cautions:
- If you need on-prem inference to satisfy security constraints we can discuss a short private deployment evaluation, but for speed the hosted sandbox is recommended.
- We will provide a binding for function/tool calls that retries idempotently if your reranker returns transient 5xx.

Attachment: integration_schema_v1.json (sample request/response shape for reranker callback)

Proposed kickoff: May 22 — Redwood will run a 30m tech alignment on May 21 (90 minutes UTC window options: 16:00–17:30 UTC). Let me know what works for Marcus.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
